page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256g-1920s is a memory-optimized server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 32 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 16 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 1920 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities across memory and processing tasks. The server achieves a top-tier rating in large-block memory write bandwidth at 193.78 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 40.79 GB/sec. Passmark memory testing places the system in the top tier with a score of 2989.67. Single-core stress-ng performance is strong, while multi-core stress-ng performance is average. Database operations and Redis SET operations demonstrate strong throughput, handling 63.9 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance delivers high resource density, particularly in memory allocation and local NVMe storage, without the premium of GPU hardware. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance, though the 2.0 GHz clock speed represents a tradeoff compared to high-frequency compute-optimized instances. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is strong at 293.61 GB/sec, but cached small-block memory read bandwidth remains average.

This server is suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database deployments, and data processing tasks. The combination of 256.0 GB RAM and 1920 GB NVMe SSD supports high-throughput static web serving, Redis caching layers, and medium-sized LLM inference tasks, where it achieves 30.26 tokens/sec for text generation on 7B models.
